title: Oviposition by mutualistic seed-parasitic pollinators and its effects on annual fitness of single- and multi-flowered host plants
screening_reason: Annual seed output and Chiastocheta oviposition/seed predation are measured across Trollius floral architectures and altitudes, but the focal exposure is flower number/size and fly abundance rather than explicit plant-fly temporal matching.
notes: Hemborg & Després 1999; strong cost/benefit and final-fitness context across Sweden and the Alps.

title: Evolution of oviposition strategies and speciation in the globeflower flies Chiastocheta spp. (Anthomyiidae)
screening_reason: Six Chiastocheta species partition oviposition across flower ages/days and generate outcomes from mutualistic to parasitic, but this is within-flower-age resource partitioning rather than population-level plant-partner phenological synchrony tied to final plant fitness.
notes: Després & Jaeger 1999; direct evidence that interaction sign depends on fly species and visit/oviposition timing within flower longevity.

title: Stability of floral specialization in Trollius europaeus in contrasting ecological environments
screening_reason: Experimental flower opening changes Chiastocheta and co-pollinator visitation and net seed set, but the manipulated axis is floral architecture rather than temporal matching.
notes: Ibáñez et al. 2009; net seed set + pollinator community context, no synchrony estimand.

title: Selective flower abortion maintains moth cooperation in a newly discovered pollination mutualism
screening_reason: Glochidion acuminatum seed production and Epicephala egg load/ovule damage are quantitatively linked, including a 16% seed-production benefit of selective abortion, but temporal matching is not the focal exposure.
notes: Goto et al. 2010; strong net-fitness mechanism in Glochidion-Epicephala, useful because timing is missing while final seed fitness is present.

title: Natural enemies and sex: how seed predators and pathogens contribute to sex-differential reproductive success in a gynodioecious plant
screening_reason: Hadena-associated pollination/oviposition and reproductive success are measured in Dianthus sylvestris, but flower size/sex morph and natural-enemy exposure are the focal axes rather than plant-moth synchrony.
notes: Collin et al. 2002; foundational Dianthus-Hadena mechanism context, biologically linked to IWE041 but not a strict timing effect.
